latest_nl_proof:
Let x be any real number, and define t = x - \lfloor x \rfloor. Then the identity x = \lfloor x \rfloor + t is immediate by rearranging the definition of t.

It remains to show that 0 \le t < 1. By the defining property of the floor function, \lfloor x \rfloor is the greatest integer less than or equal to x, so in particular
\[
\lfloor x \rfloor \le x < \lfloor x \rfloor + 1.
\]
Subtracting \lfloor x \rfloor from all three terms gives
\[
0 \le x - \lfloor x \rfloor < 1.
\]
Since t = x - \lfloor x \rfloor, we conclude that 0 \le t < 1.

Thus for every real x, if t = x - \lfloor x \rfloor, then x = \lfloor x \rfloor + t and 0 \le t < 1.
